deals.summary: A late-night web lead reaches Dana, attends a confirmed visit, supplies insurance and takes delivery before a rep-approved check-in.
Dana confirms an overnight Forester lead and hosts the visit; the insurance document remains outstanding.
Leah logs a walk-in, Sofia handles the purchase and Grace delivers the Fit that same day, with no AI messages.
Tom handles a same-day walk-in purchase; Grace is waiting for the final handover paperwork, with no AI involvement.
Arjun sends an approved AI draft, supplies the Golf quote, follows up after three silent days and completes the sale.
Sofia handles an email-only draft workflow and follows up on the Elantra quote after three days; the buyer is considering it.
Aisha contacts Sofia through two channels; Karen transfers the sick rep’s deal and callback to Tom, who completes the sale.
Callum reaches Dana’s mobile after emailing the store; Karen moves the sick rep’s deal and callback to Arjun, and a visit is confirmed.
A missed call receives a prompt text, Dana confirms a visit, and a friendly no-show follow-up brings Dylan back to buy.
Sofia confirms a missed-call lead who no-shows; a friendly follow-up produces a new confirmed appointment, despite an earlier AI price guess.
Dana quotes a Corolla, two follow-ups go unanswered, and a day-45 check-in revives the dormant buyer before delivery.
Tom’s Escape quote goes quiet after two AI follow-ups; a day-45 check-in revives Keira and Karen transfers the work to Sofia.
Karen chases an unlogged visit; Arjun backfills it, Omar waits a week for income evidence and email reminders lead to delivery.
Karen discovers an unlogged Outlander visit and transfers Tom’s work to Sofia; Omar is still waiting after a week of email reminders.
After a visit and trade appraisal, Nikhil finds the payment too high, receives a pushy AI reply and buys elsewhere.
Olivia’s trade appraisal leaves the payment too high; Karen transfers Tom’s follow-up to Arjun while the buyer considers another dealer.
Parker opts out by SMS but receives both an AI text and a staff email; a second deal also contains later prohibited contact.
Quinn opts out by email; a later AI SMS and Tom’s call both violate the buyer’s request.
Parker’s older Camry enquiry shares the CR-V buyer record; its pre-opt-out AI message is allowed but a later staff email is prohibited.
The AI treats Rhea’s requested visit as certain and invents a payment; Arjun later confirms a replacement visit and completes the sale.
The AI calls Samir’s requested visit settled; Sofia handles his human request, corrects the error and confirms an upcoming replacement.
The AI guarantees a truck sold the day before; Dana explains, and Tessa declines the alternatives.
The AI guarantees a sold Ram, then ignores Uri’s human and pricing requests without any later human event or task; the enquiry remains unresolved.
With email AI off and no owner, Vera waits two days, tries SMS and receives robotic non-answers instead of a human or quote.
Wes’s email stays unanswered with email AI off; a later missed-call text invents a price and promises a person without recording any handoff.
A fictional SEO vendor emails the store; Leah identifies the spam and closes it without AI contact.
An SEO vendor receives an inappropriate canned AI auto-reply before Leah classifies the message as not a buyer.
Sofia quoted Yvonne and two follow-ups went unanswered; the enquiry remains dormant after 26 days, with no follow-up due.
Zane has been silent for 44 days after Tom’s quote and two AI follow-ups, including an unsupported payment; Tom’s day-45 callback is due tomorrow.
